ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, November 1, 2026 — Key Takeaways:
- "Russian forces lost ground on the battlefield in October 2026 for the second month in a row."
- "Russian forces suffered their highest monthly losses of the war thus far in October 2026, paying a growing price for their territorial losses."
- "Russian forces have managed to make marginal advances in the Dobropillya direction by committing substantial resources and personnel, but the seizure of Dobropillya would not enable sweeping Russian advances in Donetsk Oblast."
- "Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi has had cascading effects on Russian offensives against the Fortress Belt directly from the east."
- "Russian forces have not yet completed the seizure of Kostyantynivka over a year after first infiltrating into the town."
- "Ukraine and Turkey are advancing joint cooperation to support a limited ceasefire in the Black Sea and secure the maritime security of global grain exports."
Also (search snippet): Russian forces are largely deprioritizing offensive operations in the Kupyansk and Borova directions following the recent successful Ukrainian operations Vivaldi and Veles. Russian forces continue limited offensive efforts to expand their claimed "buffer zone" along the international border in northern Sumy and Kharkiv oblasts but have achieved only localized tactical gains.
